html:
The Highway of Death was a road north of Kuwait City where, on 26 and 27 February 1991, coalition aircraft attacked a long column of retreating Iraqi vehicles at the end of the Gulf War.

As the ground war began and the Iraqi army collapsed, thousands of vehicles streamed north on Highway 80 toward Basra. Many carried loot from Kuwait. US and allied aircraft bombed the front and rear of the column, trapping it, then struck the stalled vehicles. Hundreds of vehicles were destroyed. The number of dead is disputed, with estimates from a few hundred up to over a thousand.

Photographs of the burned wrecks shocked many viewers. Some called it a slaughter of men who were fleeing. Others said they were still armed units and a legitimate target. The pictures are sometimes said to have helped persuade President George H. W. Bush to end the fighting after about 100 hours of ground war, on 28 February.

Saddam survived in power. Within days his army was turned on rebels in the 1991 uprisings.
sum: The Highway of Death was a road north of Kuwait City where, on 26 and 27 February 1991, coalition aircraft attacked a long column of retreating Iraqi vehicles at the end of the Gulf War.
